\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کسل} \fa{کننده} (kesel-konande)}{کسل کننده (kesel-konande)}]{\fa{کسل} \fa{کننده} (kesel-konande) — boring}

\label{lesson:FA-C273-kesel-konande}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for pink, then the Persian for dark.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کسل} \fa{کننده}}
\textbf{\fa{کسل} \fa{کننده}} — \emph{kesel-konande} — \textquotedblleft{}boring\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{kesel-konande} is \textquotedblleft{}making weary\textquotedblright{}: \emph{kesel}, \textquotedblleft{}weary, bored\textquotedblright{}, is borrowed from Arabic \emph{kasal}, \textquotedblleft{}sluggishness\textquotedblright{} (root \emph{k-s-l}, Lane), and \emph{konande}, \textquotedblleft{}making\textquotedblright{}, is from \emph{kardan}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for this chapter.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for pink, then the Persian for dark, then say \emph{kesel-konande} again
\end{itemize}
